components.name: Prior-weighted normalization and exponential reweighting
components.operation: Normalize current weights to select the allocation, then multiply each weight by beta to the observed coordinate loss.

variants.cost: Feedback: T complete vectors, containing NT scalar losses; not T scalar bandit observations. Direct implementation accounting: each round uses an N-coordinate summation, normalization, dot product and N multiplicative updates, including N evaluations of beta^ell_i^t. Thus O(N) scalar arithmetic plus N power evaluations per round and O(N) working storage; initialization costs O(N). These are counts of the displayed operations, not a source bit-complexity theorem. Generating strategy losses and the precision/cost of powers are charged separately and are not declared free.
variants.implementation_details_ref: PDF/printed p.4 Figure 1 and Equations (1)–(2); p.2 protocol
variants.name: Figure 1 Hedge(beta), 0<beta<1
variants.output: The sequence of allocations p^t in the probability simplex, one before each feedback vector. Performance concerns the incurred mixture loss sum_t p^t dot ell^t. There is no terminal point estimate or sampled-action realized-loss guarantee in this extraction. Zero-prior coordinates receive zero allocation throughout.
public_inputs: Positive integer number of strategies N
Positive integer number of trials T
Initial vector w^1 in [0,1]^N with sum_i w_i^1=1
variants.query_and_update: For t=1,...,T: compute W_t=sum_j w_j^t and choose p_i^t=w_i^t/W_t; receive the complete ell^t; incur h_t=sum_i p_i^t ell_i^t; update every coordinate w_i^{t+1}=w_i^t beta^{ell_i^t}. Because beta>0, positive weights remain positive and zero weights remain zero, so W_t stays positive for every finite trial.
variants.requirements: Each round reveals the entire ell^t in [0,1]^N after allocation p^t is selected. The environment may choose losses adaptively, including as a function of current p^t. This is the source's mixture-loss protocol.
variants.state_and_initialization: Store w^1. Initial weights may be zero, but at least one is positive because they sum to one. No later normalization of stored weights is required.
variants.tuning_and_stopping: Choose beta before the run and hold it fixed. Perform exactly T rounds. The selected guarantee holds for every beta in (0,1); it does not require advance knowledge of comparator loss. Section 2.2's optimized tuning and its extra information requirements are not part of this variant's extracted performance.
